message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I have a $1385 cash balance and am on VENTNOR_AVENUE. My holdings include an unmortgaged brown monopoly, fully built pink and orange monopolies, and several mortgaged properties.

I have two get-out-of-jail cards. The opponent has $20 and is on ILLINOIS_AVENUE with a mortgaged Pennsylvania Railroad, partially built reds, and no GOOJF cards. Players three and four are bankrupt. The bank has one house and twelve hotels remaining. NORTH_CAROLINA_AVENUE is unowned.

Baltic was already unmortgaged this turn. The brown monopoly is now fully available with zero houses. I will build one house on Baltic to exhaust the bank's last house. This leaves enough cash to cover the opponent's red houses.

The opponent has only $20, so they cannot buy a house immediately. After passing GO, they would have $220, enough to purchase one red house and jump from two to three houses. That would significantly increase rent on the reds.

The opponent's red houses would jump from $250 to $700 in rent if they buy one house after passing GO. Purchasing the last house on Baltic now costs $50 and leaves $1335 in cash. This exhausts the bank's final house immediately, preventing the opponent from building any red houses.

I will not build hotels on the orange or pink monopolies. Selling houses would return them to the bank, allowing the opponent to purchase them.

Unmortgaging the light blue properties would cost too much. The mortgage values total roughly $160 plus house costs. Building on Baltic is cheaper and more effective.

The opponent will roll from Illinois Avenue next. They could land on B&O Railroad, Atlantic Avenue, or Ventnor Avenue. All three are mortgaged and worth nothing.

The opponent's next roll from Illinois Avenue could land on Water Works, Marvin Gardens, Go to Jail, or the unowned North Carolina Avenue. They will not hit my pink or orange monopolies this turn. The only way they could pay me large rent is if a Chance or Community Chest card moves them onto those properties.

The opponent cannot pass GO from Illinois Avenue this turn. The maximum roll of twelve lands on Chance. A Chance card advancing to GO would give them $200, bringing their total to $220 and allowing them to purchase a house.

I will not trade. The opponent has no properties I want, and their red houses are too dangerous.
